gaps.text: In-line measurement of Product temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion joins NIR and Raman into one model, beginning with block scaling of the concatenated spectra so neither method dominates. Both probes must look at the same small spot on the flowing product, and the two acquisition rates must be aligned to a common time step. The fused model is only worth keeping if it beats the best single method on independent batches, with each instrument calibrated and maintained separately.)
In-line accuracy, detection limit and response-time figures for fat and protein in this concentrated milk matrix are not covered by the supplied sources.
No supplied source states an achievable fiber-link length for the specific configuration at this process point.

items.finding: The source notes that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform whether product temperature needs to be monitored or controlled during in-line NIR/MIR measurement, and whether temperature effects should be tested in the comparison experiment.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns aqueous solutions and tempered sample holders, not an in-line product temperature sensor; transfer to a concentrated milk matrix on a process line is uncertain.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: The source describes low-level data fusion as the simplest way to combine inputs by rearranging variables from different sources into a new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform a practical comparison experiment that starts with concatenated NIR and Raman variables, then checks whether the fused model outperforms the best single method on independent batches.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a general PAT data-fusion review, not a concentrated milk or in-line NIR/Raman study; block scaling, spot alignment, and time-step alignment are not addressed here.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: The source states that before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate each dataset's contribution to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports a staged assessment: first evaluate NIR and Raman separately, then fuse only if each method adds complementary information for the composition changes of interest.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general data-fusion recommendation, not specific to concentrated milk or in-line probes; complementarity may differ with matrix, process conditions, and instrument setup.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82
